children.text: 1 samādhiḥ araṇasaraṇasarvasamavasaraṇo nāma samādhiḥ anilāniketaratir nāma samādhiḥ tathatāsthitaniścitto nāma samādhiḥ kāyakalipramathano nāma samādhiḥ
children.translated_text: a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called 'Refuge and Resort of Peaceful Gathering of All,' a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Delight in the Homeless Wind,' a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Mind Established in <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness),' a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Crushing of Bodily Impurity,'

children.text:
ganakalpo
2 nāma samādhiḥ ākāśasaṃgamvimuktanirupalepo nāma samādhiḥ ime te hy āvusa śāradvatīputra samādhayo bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānāṃ yeṣu khalu
children.translated_text: a <s>samādhi</s> called '[Mental] Impurity like [mere] Conceptualization.' A <s>samādhi</s> called 'Free from Attachment to Space, without Stain.' These indeed, friend <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the <s>samādhis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>, in which

children.text: 3 bodhisatvo mahāsatvo kṣipram anuttarāṃ saṃyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbotsyati | anyāni cāprameyāṇy asaṃkhyeyāni samādhimukhāni dhāraṇimukhāni ca | yatra śikṣamāṇāḥ bodhisatvā
children.translated_text: a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> will quickly attain supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And there are other immeasurable, innumerable gates of <s>samādhi</s> and gates of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mnemonic formulae), in which training, the <s>bodhisattvas</s>

children.text: 4 kṣipram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhyanti | athāyuṣmāṃ subhūtir āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputram etad avocat* vyākṛto batāyam āvusa śāradvatīputra bodhisatvo mahāsatvo
children.translated_text: quickly attain supreme perfect awakening. Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: 'This <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should be known as having been predicted

children.text: 5 pūrvakair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau ye 'py etarhi daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālikāsameṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatāḥ arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās tiṣṭhanti
children.translated_text: by former <s>arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, for supreme perfect awakening. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones who now exist in the world-realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River in the ten directions,

children.text: 6 te 'pi tathāgatās taṃ bodhisatvaṃ mahāsatvaṃ idānīṃ vyākurvanti | yaḥ khalv imeṣu samādhiṣu viharati na ca ka
children.translated_text: those <s>Tathāgatas</s> also are now predicting that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> [for supreme awakening], who indeed dwells in these <s>samādhis</s> and does not per-
and does not think by means of these <s>samādhis</s>:

children.text: 7 punar bodhisatvā asamāpannā | ahaṃ punaḥ samāpannaḥ samāpadyāmi samāpatsyāmi ca | sarve te tasya khalu vi
children.translated_text: other <s>bodhisattvas</s> have not attained [these samādhis]. But I have attained, am attaining, and will attain [them].' All those dis-
cursive thoughts are not found [in him],
do not arise [in him]. Thus spoken, the venerable <s>Śāradvatī-</s>

yuṣmantaṃ
8 subhūtim etad avocat* tat kiṃ punar āvusa subhūte
children.translated_text: this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'But then, friend <s>Subhūti</s>,

children.text: mādhiṣu sthito bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ vyākṛto vedi
children.translated_text: <s>samādhis</s>, should the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> be known as predicted
by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and by those who
now exist in the ten directions, in the Ganges-

children.text:
kāsameṣu
9 lokadhātuṣu tathāgatās tiṣṭhanti | yāpayanti | āha no ity āvusa śāradvatīputra tat kasmād dhetor na hy āvusa śāradvatīputra anyā prajñāpāramitā anyaḥ samādhi
children.translated_text: world-realms, where <s>Tathāgatas</s> exist and endure?' He said: 'No, friend <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>. Why is that? Because, friend <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) is not one thing, the <s>samādhi</s> anoth-

children.text:
satvo
10 mahāsatvaḥ bodhisatva eva samādhiḥ samādhir eva bodhisatvaś ca samādhiś ca prajñāpāramitā āha : yady ā
children.translated_text: <s>mahāsattva</s> [yet another]. The <s>bodhisattva</s> himself is the <s>samādhi</s>; the <s>samādhi</s> itself is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Both the <s>samādhi</s> and the <s>bodhisattva</s> are the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' He said: 'If, friend <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>samādhi</s> is not one thing

children.text: samādhir yaś ca bodhisatvas tau khalu prajñāpāramitā | tan na punaḥ
children.translated_text: both the <s>samādhi</s> and the <s>bodhisattva</s> are the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, then [the <s>bodhisattva</s>] does not
know the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> through the <s>samādhi</s>,
nor does he perceive [it]?' He said: 'By a certain

children.text: 1 śāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ tāṃ sarvadharmasamatāṃ tena samādhinā na jānāti | nāpi saṃjānāti tat kasmād dhetor āha : avidyāmānatvād eva tasya bodhisat
children.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> does not know the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> through that <s>samādhi</s>, nor does he perceive [it]. Why is that? He said: 'Because of the very non-existence of that <s>bodhisat-</s>

children.text: 2 ca samādhes tasyāś ca prajñāpāramitāyāḥ na jānāti nāpi saṃjānāti | atha bhagavān āyuṣmate subhūtaye sādhukāram adāsīt sādhu sādhu subhūte : subhāṣiteṣā vāk
children.translated_text: <s>samādhi</s>, and of that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he neither knows nor perceives [it].' Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Well said, well said, <s>Subhūti</s>! This speech is well-spoken,

children.text: 3 tva mayā araṇāvihāriṇāṃ śrāvakānām agratāyā nirdiṣṭaḥ tasya te pratirūpo 'yam upadeśaḥ evaṃ ca bodhisatvena mahāsatvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratā śikṣitavyaṃ | e
children.translated_text: you were designated by me as foremost among <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) who dwell in peaceful [meditation]. This instruction is befitting you. Thus indeed should a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Like-

children.text:
ramitāyāṃ
4 vīryapāramitāyāṃ | kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ | śīlapāramitāyāṃ | dānapāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ | evaṃ smṛtyupasthāneṣu śikṣitavyaṃ | yāvad āryāṣṭaṃgamā
children.translated_text: (Perfection of Meditation), the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Effort), the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience), the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Morality), the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Giving), one should train. Likewise in the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) one should train, up to the Noble Eight-

children.text: 5 tathāgatabaleṣu | peyālaṃ yāvad aṣṭādaśasv āvedanikeṣu buddhadharmeṣu śikṣitavyam iti | athāyuṣmāṃ śāradvatīputro bhagavantam etad avocat* evaṃ śi
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s powers — [abbreviated passage] — up to the eighteen unique qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, one should train.' Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Training thus, vener-

children.text: 6 bhagavan bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣati | bhagavān āha : evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāradvatīputra bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ
children.translated_text: does the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Training thus, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> trains in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,

children.text: 7 tac cānupalaṃbhayogena | evaṃ yāvad dānapāramitāyāṃ śikṣati | peyālaṃ | evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ smṛtyupasthāneṣu śikṣati | yāvad evaṃ śikṣamāṇo yāvad aṣṭāda
children.translated_text: and that by the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalaṃbhayoga</s>). Likewise he trains in the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> — [abbreviated passage]. Likewise, training thus, he trains in the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness); up to: thus training, up to the eight-

children.text:
keṣu
8 buddhadharmeṣu śikati | tac cānupalaṃbhayogeneti | athāyuṣmāṃ śāradvatīputro bhagavantam etad avocat* evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bhadanta bhagavan bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ prajñāpāramitā
children.translated_text: of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, he trains — and that by the method of non-apprehension.' Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Training thus, venerable Blessed One, does the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>

children.text:
9 śikṣaty anupalaṃbhayogeneti | bhagavān āha: evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāradvatīputra bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣaty anupalaṃbhayogeneti | āha : kiṃ bhadanta
10 bhagavan nopalabhate | bhagavān āha : ātmānaṃ nopalabhate | satvaṃ nopalabhate | yāvaj jānakapaśyakaṃ nopalabhate | atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya | tathā skandhān nopalabhate
children.translated_text: by the method of non-apprehension?' The Blessed One said: 'Training thus, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> trains in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> by the method of non-apprehension.' He said: 'What, venerable Blessed One, does he not apprehend?' The Blessed One said: 'He does not apprehend the self; he does not apprehend a being; up to: he does not apprehend the knower and seer — on account of their absolute purity. Likewise he does not apprehend the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates);

children.text: 11 nopalabhate hy āyatanāni nopalabhate | atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya | tathā avidyān nopalabhate yāvaj jarāmaraṇaṃ nopalabhate | atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya | evaṃ
children.translated_text: he does not apprehend; the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) he does not apprehend — on account of their absolute purity. Likewise he does not apprehend ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), up to: he does not apprehend old age and death — on account of their absolute purity. Thus

children.text:
1 duḥkhaṃ nopalabhate | samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ mārgaṃ nopalabhate | atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya | evaṃ kāmadhātuṃ rūpadhātum ārūpyadhātum nḥpalabhate | atynataviśuddhitām upādāya |
2 tathā smṛtyupasthānāni nopalabhate | yāvad āryāṣṭāṅgaṃ mārgaṃ nopalabhate atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya | tathā daśa tathāgatabalāni nopalabhate | yāvad aṣṭādaśāvedanikān –aṣṭādaśāveṇikān
3 buddhadharmān nopalabhate | atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya | ṣaṭ pāramitāṃ nopalabhate | atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya | śrotāpannaṃ nopalabhate atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya |
children.translated_text: he does not apprehend suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>); he does not apprehend origination, cessation, or the path — on account of their absolute purity. Likewise he does not apprehend the desire-realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), the form-realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), or the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>) — on account of their absolute purity. Likewise he does not apprehend the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>); up to: he does not apprehend the Noble Eightfold Path — on account of their absolute purity. Likewise he does not apprehend the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers; up to: he does not apprehend the eighteen unique qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — on account of their absolute purity. He does not apprehend the six <s>pāramitās</s> — on account of their absolute purity. He does not apprehend the stream-enterer (<s>śrotāpanna</s>) — on account of their absolute purity.

children.text: 4 sakṛdāgāminam anāgāminam arhantaṃ nopalabhate | atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya | pratyekabuddhaṃ nopalabhate bodhisatvaṃ nopalabhate tathāgataṃ nopalabhate atyantaviśuddhi
children.translated_text: he does not apprehend the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), the non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), or the <s>arhat</s> — on account of their absolute purity. He does not apprehend the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one); he does not apprehend the <s>bodhisattva</s>; he does not apprehend the <s>Tathāgata</s> — on account of their absolute

yeti |

children.translated_text: [any of these].' Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'What, vener-
able Blessed One, is that purity?'

children.text: 6 avyavadānam aprādurbhāvo anupalaṃbho anabhisaṃskāraḥ sarvadharmāṇām eṣā sā viśuddhir iti | āha : evaṃ punar bhadanta bhagavan śikṣamāṇo bodhisatvo
children.translated_text: non-purification, non-manifestation, non-apprehension, non-fabrication of all <s>dharmas</s> — that is that purity.' He said: 'But, venerable Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva</s> training thus,

children.text: 7 katameṣu dharmeṣu śikṣito bhavati bhagavān āha : evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ śāradvatīputra bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ
children.translated_text: in which <s>dharmas</s> is he trained?' The Blessed One said: 'Training thus, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>

children.text: id dharmeṣu śikṣito bhavati | tat kasmād dhetor na hy ete śāradvatīpu
children.translated_text: in any <s>dharmas</s> whatsoever. Why is that? Because, <s>Śāradvatī-</s>

children.translated_text: these <s>dharmas</s> do not exist in the way that these foolish ordinary persons (<s>bālapṛthagjanas</s>) are attached [to them].' He said: 'But how, venerable Blessed One, do these <s>dharmas</s> exist,

|

children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'In the way they do not exist, in that way they exist. Being thus non-existent, they are called ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>).' He said:

children.text: ha : rūpaṃ śāradvatīputra na saṃvidyate adhyātmaśūnyatām upādāya | yāvad abhāvasvabhāva
children.translated_text: said: 'Form (<s>rūpa</s>), <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, does not exist — on account of inner emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>); up to: on account of emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature

tmaśūnyatām
11 upādāya | yāvad abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatām upādāya | evaṃ smṛtyupasthānāni na saṃvidyante |
children.translated_text: emptiness, up to: on account of emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature. Likewise, the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>) do not exist —

children.text: peyālaṃ | yāvad aṣṭādaśavedanikā buddhadharmā na saṃvidyante
children.translated_text: [abbreviated passage] — up to: the eighteen unique qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> do not exist,

children.text: 1 adhyātmaśūnyatām upādāya. yāvad abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatām upādāya | yatra bālapṛthagjanā avidyāvaśenā tṛṣṇāśābhiniviṣṭās tebhir vidyā kalpitā : avidyābhi
children.translated_text: on account of inner emptiness, up to: on account of emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature. Wherein foolish ordinary persons, under the power of ignorance, are attached through craving and hope — by them knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) is fabricated. Being over-
attached to both of the two extremes,

children.text: saktāḥ yadutocchedasāśvatayos te ca na jānanti na paśyanti | ye ca dharmā na saṃvidyante | tān dharmān kalpayanti | kalpayitvā ca nāmarūpe 'bhiniviṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: namely annihilationism and eternalism. And they neither know nor see. Those <s>dharmas</s> that do not exist — those <s>dharmas</s> they fabricate. And having fabricated [them], they are attached to name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) —

children.text: 3 yāvad aṣṭādaśasv āvedanikeṣu buddhadharmeṣv abhiniviṣṭāḥ eva samānāḥ asaṃvidyamānān dharmān parikalpayanti | tā ca na jānanti | na paśyanti | kiṃ te na jānanti na paśyanti
children.translated_text: up to: being attached to the eighteen unique qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, being thus, they fabricate non-existent <s>dharmas</s>. And they neither know nor see. What do they not know, not see?

children.text:
*{āvedanikeṣu for āveṇikeṣu}*
4 jānanti paśyanti | evaṃ vedanāṃ saṃjñāṃ saṃskārāṃ vijñānaṃ na jānanti na paśyanti | peyālaṃ | yāvad aṣṭādaśāvedanikān buddhadharmān na jānanti na paśyanti | yasmāc ca na jānanti na budhyanti |
children.translated_text: *{unique [qualities] for āveṇika}* know or see. Likewise feeling, perception, volitions, consciousness — they do not know, do not see. [Abbreviated passage.] Up to: the eighteen unique qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> they do not know, do not see. And because they do not know, do not understand,

children.text:
pṛthagjanā
5 iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchanti | te na niryānti | kutra na niryānti | kāmadhātvaiśvarye | tathā rūpadhātāv ārūpyadhātau na niryānti | śrāvakapratyekabuddhadharmeṣu na ni
children.translated_text: ordinary persons — they go by that designation. And they do not escape. From where do they not escape? From the sovereignty of the desire-realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>). Likewise from the form-realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) and formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>) they do not escape. From the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> they do not

children.text: 6 bodhisatvadharmeṣu na niryānti | samyaksaṃbuddhadharmeṣu na niryānti | te ca na śraddadhanti | kiṃ te na śraddadhanti | rūpaṃ rūpaśūnyatāṃ ca na śraddadhanti | evaṃ vedanāṃ vedanāśū
children.translated_text: From the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> they do not escape. From the <s>dharmas</s> of perfect <s>Buddhas</s> they do not escape. And they do not have faith. In what do they not have faith? They do not have faith in form and in the emptiness of form. Likewise in feeling and in the emptiness of feel-

children.translated_text: in perception and in the emptiness of perception, in volitions and in the emptiness of volitions, in consciousness and in the emptiness of consciousness they do not have faith. Up to: in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and the [emptiness of the <s>Buddha</s>-]<s>dharmas</s> they do not have faith. And furthermore they do not become established. Where do they

tiṣṭhanti |

children.translated_text: [Fragment 1 (SI P/147a1)] Verso: [1] ...the end is cut off... this is the final limit that is designated. He said: 'Own...' [2] ...The Blessed One said: 'So it is, O <s>Subhūti</s>, just as you say — emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>)...' [3] ...this situation exists. However, O <s>Subhūti</s>, what you say — all are [empty by] the emptiness of own-characteristics...' [4] ...among all <s>dharmas</s> that are empty, the first and last limits are known. And further, O <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhi</s>-[sattva]... [5] ...among all empty <s>dharmas</s>, while practicing, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not cling to any <s>dharma</s>... [6] ...whether <s>śrāvaka</s>-dharmas or <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-dharmas or <s>Tathāgata</s>-dharmas. Thus... [7] ...it is called. For what reason is it called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? The Blessed One said: 'The supreme...' [8] ...it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. However, O <s>Subhūti</s>, by this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>... [9] ...have gone to the other shore of all <s>dharmas</s>, in due proportion; for that reason it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. However, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the supreme... [10] ...the other shore is not apprehended. For that reason it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. However, O <s>Subhūti</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>... [11] ...for that reason it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. However, O <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not conjoined with any <s>dharma</s>, nor disconjoined... Recto: [1] ...for that reason it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And for what reason? For thus, O <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is formless (<s>arūpin</s>), without indication (<s>anidarśana</s>)... [2] ...the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>... the conduct of... of all eloquences, of all happinesses, it abandons the three worlds... [3] ...or by deities, or by any persons who follow the vehicle of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and whatever others... [4] ...for what reason? For thus, O <s>Subhūti</s>, ...all <s>dharmas</s> are not apprehended here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. [5] ...one should practice. Furthermore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, in this profound... [6] ...one should practice for the purpose of knowledge of suffering, its origin, cessation, and the path. Likewise, [for the knowledge] of the origin of suffering... [7] ...for the purpose of knowledge of destruction, non-arising, and the knowledge of the nature of things, one should practice... [8] ...<s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'If, Blessed One, ... the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>...' [9] ...He said: 'Here, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, in this profound...' [10] ...one should practice. 'Samādhi (concentration) is of no purpose to me; therein I should not practice...' [11] ...or purpose or no purpose.

children.text:
Fragm. 2 (SI P/147a1)
V1 vijñānaṃ me cārthaṃ vānarthaṃ vā na cartavyaṃ | evaṃ dānapāramitā yāvat prajñāpāramitā me ... yāvat sarvākārajñatā me cārthaṃ vānarthaṃ vā na cartavyaṃ ///
children.translated_text: [Fragment 2] Verso: [1] 'Consciousness is of neither purpose nor no purpose to me; I should not practice [regarding it]. Likewise, the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Giving) up to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>... up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) is of neither purpose nor no purpose to me; I should not practice [regarding it].'

children.text: 2 ... anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā na kaścid dharmaṃ parimṛśyamānopalabdho yo 'rthaṃ vā kuryād api tu subhūter utpādād vā tathāgatānām anutpādād vā ///
children.translated_text: [2] '...having fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), no <s>dharma</s> being grasped at is apprehended which would serve a purpose. However, O <s>Subhūti</s>, whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise...'

children.text: 3 sthitaiva dharmaṇān dharmatā sā ca na kasyacid arthaṃ vānarthaṃ vā karoti. evaṃ ca subhūte bodhisatvena mahāsatvenārthānartho parivarjya satataṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caritavyaṃ ///
children.translated_text: [3] '...the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) of <s>dharmas</s> remains standing. And that [nature] neither serves a purpose for anything nor fails to serve a purpose. Thus, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having set aside [considerations of] purpose and non-purpose, should constantly practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

children.text: 4 evam uktāyuṣmāṃ subhūtir bhagavantam etad avovat : kena kāraṇena bhadanta bhagavan prajñāpāramitā na kasyacid dharmasyārthakartrī. bhagavān āha : ///
children.translated_text: [4] Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'For what reason, Reverend Blessed One, is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> not the accomplisher of purpose for any <s>dharma</s>?' The Blessed One said:

children.text: 5 hy asamskṛtadharmāvatāraṇāṃ tena kāraṇena na kasyacid dharmasyārthakartrī nāpy anarthakartrī. āha : nanu bhadanta bhagavann asaṃskṛtaparamārthaṃ sa ///

Just as neither the eastern direction of space is known, nor the southern, nor the western, nor the northern direction is known, nor the upward direction, nor the lower direction, nor the intermediate directions are known — even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, neither is the eastern direction [of that vehicle] known, nor the southern, nor the western, nor the northern direction is known, nor the upward direction, nor the lower direction, nor the intermediate directions are known. 3 teṣām api varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ ātmanā ca śīlaṃ rakṣati / paraṃ ca śīle samādapayati / śīlasya ca varṇaṃ bhāṣate ye py anye śīlaṃ rakṣanti
4 teṣām api varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ evam ātmanā ca kṣāntiṃ bhāvayati paraṃ ca kṣāntau samādāpayati kṣānteś ca varṇaṃ bhāṣate / ye 'py anye kṣāntiṃ bhāvayanti teṣām api varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ
5 ātmanā ca vīryam ārabhate paraṃ ca vīrye samādāpayati / vīryasya ca varṇaṃ bhāṣate / ye 'py anye vīryam ārabhante teṣāṃ ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ // ātmanā ca samādhiṃ samāpadyante
6 paraṃ ca samādhau samādāpayati / samādheś ca varṇaṃ bhāṣate ye 'py anye samādhiṃ samāpadyante teṣāṃ ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ // ātmanā ca prajñāṃ bhāvayati
7 paraṃ prajñāyāṃ samādāpayati / prajñāyāś ca varṇaṃ bhāṣate ye 'py anye prajñāṃ bhāvayanti / teṣāṃ ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ // yāvad ātmanā ca daśakuśalān karmapathāṃ samādāya vartante
6 paraṃ ca daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu samādāpayati / daśānāṃ ca kuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate / ye 'py anye satvā daśakuśalān karmapathān samādāya vartante teṣāṃ ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ
children.translated_text:
[AdP (Conze 70f.)]
1 ...thus he delights them with dharmas that do not [truly] exist. And he does not apprehend the perception of beings. 'Alas, these beings who perceive substance in what is without substance!' Thus indeed, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not see any <s>dharma</s> as separated from <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of dharmas),
2 practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), and does not apprehend a being, nor the designation of a being. He himself practices giving (<s>dāna</s>), and establishes others in giving, and praises the virtue of giving. Those other beings who also practice giving —
3 of them too he speaks in praise and approbation. He himself guards moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and establishes others in moral conduct, and praises the virtue of moral conduct. Those others who also guard moral conduct —
4 of them too he speaks in praise and approbation. Thus he himself cultivates patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), and establishes others in patience, and praises the virtue of patience. Those others who also cultivate patience — of them too he speaks in praise and approbation.
5 He himself undertakes vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), and establishes others in vigor, and praises the virtue of vigor. Those others who also undertake vigor — of them too he speaks in praise and approbation. He himself enters into concentration (<s>samādhi</s>),
6 and establishes others in concentration, and praises the virtue of concentration. Those others who also enter into concentration — of them too he speaks in praise and approbation. He himself cultivates wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>),
7 and establishes others in wisdom, and praises the virtue of wisdom. Those others who also cultivate wisdom — of them too he speaks in praise and approbation. Furthermore, he himself abides having undertaken the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśakuśalakarmapatha</s>),
6 and establishes others in the ten wholesome courses of action, and praises the virtue of the ten wholesome courses of action. Those other beings who also abide having undertaken the ten wholesome courses of action — of them too he speaks in praise and approbation.

children.text:
C. AdP (Conze 71)
1 ātmanā cāṣṭāṅgasamanvāgataṃ poṣadham upavasti / paraṃ cāṣṭāṅgasamanvāgate poṣadhe samādāpayati / aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatasya ca poṣadhasya varṇaṃ bhāṣate / ye cānye satvā aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgataṃ poṣadham upavasanti
2 teṣāṃ ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ // ātmanā ca pañcaśikṣāpadāni samādāya vartante / paraṃ ca pañcasu śikṣāpadeṣu samādāpayanti / pañcānāṃ ca śikṣāpadānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate / ye 'py anye satvā pañca śikṣāpadāni samādāpya vartante
3 teṣāṃ ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ // evam ātmanā ca prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate / yāvac caturthaṃ maitrīṃ karuṇāṃ muditām upekṣāṃ ākāśānantyāyatanasamāpattiṃ yāvan naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattiṃ
4 ātmanā ca smṛtyupasthānāni bhāvayati / yāvad āryāṣṭāṅgaṃ mārgaṃ trīṇi vimokṣamukhāny aṣṭau vimokṣān navānupūrvasamāpattī daśatathāgatabalāni
5 catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvido mahāmaitrīṃ mahākaruṇām aṣṭādaśāveṇikāṃ buddhadharmān aśītim anuvyañjanāni bhāvayati / paraṃ cāśītyāṃ anuvyañjaneṣu samādāpayati | aśītir anuvyañjanānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate
6 ye 'py anye satvā aśītim anuvyañjanāni bhāvayanti teṣāṃ ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ // yadi subhūte dharmadhātur yathā pūrveṇa tathā paścān na tathā madhye nābhaviṣyat
7 na bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carann upāyakauśalena satvānān dharmadhātum a sūcayiṣyate buddhakṣetraṃ ca pariśodhayiṣyate yasmād dhi subhūte dharmadhātur yathā pūrveṇa tathā paścāt tathā madhye
8 tasmād bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carann upāyakauśalena satvānāṃ dharmadhātuṃ sūcayati satvānām arthāya bodhisatvacārikāṃ carati satvāṃś ca paripācayati // sarvadharmasamatānirdeśaparivartaḥ // 74 //
children.translated_text:
[AdP (Conze 71)]
1 He himself observes the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day) endowed with the eight limbs, and establishes others in the <s>poṣadha</s> endowed with the eight limbs, and praises the virtue of the <s>poṣadha</s> endowed with the eight limbs. Those other beings who also observe the <s>poṣadha</s> endowed with the eight limbs —
2 of them too he speaks in praise and approbation. He himself abides having undertaken the five training rules (<s>pañcaśikṣāpada</s>), and establishes others in the five training rules, and praises the virtue of the five training rules. Those other beings who also abide having undertaken the five training rules —
3 of them too he speaks in praise and approbation. Thus he himself enters into the first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to the fourth, <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), the attainment of the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), up to the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>).
4 He himself cultivates the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), up to the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the three gates of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive attainments (<s>anupūrvasamāpatti</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>),
5 the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the eighteen unique <s>Buddhadharmas</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), and cultivates the eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), and establishes others in the eighty minor marks, and praises the virtue of the eighty minor marks.
6 Those other beings who also cultivate the eighty minor marks — of them too he speaks in praise and approbation. O <s>Subhūti</s>, if the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas) were not the same afterward as before, and not the same in the middle,
7 then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with skillful means, would not reveal the <s>dharmadhātu</s> to beings, nor would he purify the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). But since, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is the same afterward as before, and the same in the middle,
8 therefore the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with skillful means, reveals the <s>dharmadhātu</s> to beings, conducts the <s>bodhisattva</s>-practice for the benefit of beings, and brings beings to maturity. // The chapter on the exposition of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmasamatānirdeśaparivarta</s>) // 74 //

children.translated_text:
[AdP (Vaidya 255)]
1 ...when the exposition on the non-coming and non-going of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> was being spoken, there was a great earthquake...
2 ...it trembled, shook, and shook violently...
3 ...all those who were present bowed toward the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharmodgata</s>...
4 ...and the four great kings (<s>mahārāja</s>), always joyful...
5 ...the discourse arisen from ultimate truth, being taught and heard, was contrary to the whole world...
6 'What, O son of good family, is the cause here? What is the condition?'...
7 ...eight thousand beings obtained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>)...
8 ...the <s>dharma</s>-eyes were purified. Then...

D(ii). AdP (Vaidya 255)
1 ... buddhā bhagavantaḥ saṃmukhībhūtā bhavanti tatra tatropapadyate /
2 ... sarve cānenākṣaṇāpavivarjitā kṣaṇasaṃpadaś cāvāśīteti / tad anena tvayā subhūte paryāyenaivaṃ veditavya
3 ... tasmāt tarhi subhūte bodhisatvena mahāsatvena ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu śikṣitukāmena buddhaviṣayaṃ sarvākārajñatā
4 ... tyā dhārayitavyā paryavāptavyāḥ pravartayitavyā vācayitavyāḥ deśayitavyāḥ evaṃ satkartavyāḥ gurukartavyā
5 ... patākābhir dīpamālābhir bahuvidhābhiś ca pūjābhiḥ pūjayitavyāḥ / iyam asmākam antikād anuśāsanī / tat kasya hetoḥ
6 ... myaksaṃbodhir iti // ṛ // prajñāpāramitāyā dharmodgataparivartaḥ // ṛ //
children.translated_text:
[AdP (Vaidya 255)]
1 ...the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> appear face to face; wherever one is reborn,
2 ...and all are freed from the unfavorable conditions (<s>akṣaṇa</s>) and obtain the favorable conditions (<s>kṣaṇasaṃpad</s>). By this method, O <s>Subhūti</s>, it should be understood thus:
3 ...therefore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to train in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, [in] the domain of a <s>Buddha</s>, [and in] <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) —
4 ...should be upheld, mastered, set in motion, recited, taught, and honored and revered thus,
5 ...with banners, garlands of lamps, and various kinds of worship. 'This is our instruction from his presence. For what reason?'
6 ...[the] perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). // The <s>Dharmodgata</s> chapter of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. //
